item.title: Utah sues Stake.us operators and seeks to recover residents’ losses (2026)
item.description:
Utah sued two companies behind Stake.us on November 17, asking a judge to stop the sweepstakes casino from offering games in the state and order the companies to return money to Utah residents. The state alleges that players’ ability to redeem Stake Cash for money makes the platform’s casino games illegal gambling under Utah law.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown and the Utah Department of Commerce’s Division of Consumer Protection filed the civil suit in the Third Judicial District Court in Salt Lake County. The attorney general’s announcement names Sweepsteaks Limited and Easygo Group Holdings Pty Ltd as defendants.

Why Utah sued the companies behind Stake.us

Stake.us markets itself as a sweepstakes or social casino. Utah argues that what players can do with Stake Cash matters more than how the site describes itself. According to the attorney general’s account of the complaint, players can use the virtual currency in casino games and redeem it for money. The state alleges that the companies have operated an online casino for Utah residents since 2022.

Utah also alleges deceptive and unconscionable practices under the Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act. The state is seeking civil penalties in addition to an order to stop offering games in Utah and repayment to residents. Utah News Dispatch reported that Stake did not respond to its request for comment.

What the lawsuit means for Utah players

Stake.us added Utah to its excluded states in a November 13 terms revision, four days before Utah filed suit. The revision does not establish when access changed for existing accounts or what happens to pending prize requests.

The suit asks the court to order repayment for past activity. The filing does not establish a refund process for players. A response from either defendant or a court ruling on the requested relief would clarify what happens next.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows 11 Hotpatch Breaks App Installs and Shares a Registry Workaround (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has confirmed that the November 2026 hotpatch update for Windows 11 can break the installation and launch of some applications, including Office. The problem affects devices running Windows 11 version 24H2 and later, and Microsoft has shared a registry workaround until a fix is ready.

Affected devices show an error when installing, launching or running some apps. "Devices which installed the November 2026 hotpatch update might experience an error when installing, launching, or running some applications," Microsoft told administrators in a service alert. The error reads "ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099)" or something similar.

The problem can appear at any point, not only during installation. An app that installed and opened normally before the hotpatch can show the error later during normal use.

Which Windows 11 Devices Are Affected

The bug only hits devices that installed the November hotpatch through Windows Autopatch, Microsoft's cloud service that automates Windows and Microsoft 365 updates for businesses. Devices that installed the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates are not affected, according to Microsoft.

Microsoft says the issue appears in applications that load the 32 bit Windows Installer DLL, msi.dll. "This can happen more frequently with 32-bit applications, but can also occur for 64-bit applications under certain conditions," the company said.

Hotpatch updates install security fixes without a restart. In March, Microsoft said it would turn on hotpatch security updates by default for all eligible Windows devices managed through the Microsoft Graph API and Microsoft Intune, after the May 2026 security updates were installed. Windows Autopatch is free for customers with a Windows 10 or 11 Enterprise E3 license or higher and has been generally available since July 2022.

It is not the first Autopatch problem this year. In April, Microsoft fixed an Autopatch bug that deployed driver updates blocked by administrative policies to some managed devices belonging to customers in the European Union.

How to Apply the Hotpatch Workaround

Until a fix is available, administrators can raise the HotPatchTableSize value in the registry:

  1. Open the Start menu, type regedit and select Registry Editor.
  2. Go to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management.
  3. In the right panel, open the HotPatchTableSize value and set it to 2000. Click OK.
  4. Close Registry Editor and restart the device.

Microsoft recommends backing up the registry before making the change and making sure you know how to restore it if something goes wrong.

The hotpatch bug is the latest in a run of problems with this month's Windows updates. Microsoft has already confirmed activation failures and printing issues after the November security updates, and released emergency out of band updates earlier this week to fix the activation error 0x80041008.

Microsoft has not said when a fix for the hotpatch issue will be released.

item.title: Anthropic Starts Trading on Nasdaq After the Largest IPO in History (2026)
item.description:
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, is set to start trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT. It becomes the first publicly traded frontier AI lab, and its offering is the largest initial public offering in history.

The IPO raised about $81 billion, or more than $107 billion when private share sales are included. That beats the previous world record of $75 billion set by SpaceX in June.

Anthropic's initial valuation is roughly $1.5 trillion, below SpaceX's valuation of nearly $1.8 trillion. OpenAI has been valued at $1.25 trillion in an ongoing fundraising round.

Anthropic IPO by the Numbers

Anthropic started its roadshow last week with a plan to offer 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 a share. Its latest filing allowed for a higher price, set on Wednesday night. Its filings and reports show these figures:

  • revenue of $33.2 billion in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 1,206 percent from the year before
  • most recent quarterly sales of $17 billion, up more than 1,100 percent
  • a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of October 31
  • compute commitments of about $70.7 billion over the next 12 months
  • more than $900 billion owed to vendors over the next 19 years, mostly for data centers
  • losses of over $104 billion this year through September, largely from how it accounts for stock paid to employees
  • about $200 billion in the bank after the IPO

The number of customers spending six figures a year is up 12 times compared with a year ago.

Anthropic Warns Growth Will Slow

Anthropic revised its IPO documents on November 2 to warn investors that its growth rate will not last. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all," the revised prospectus reads. The company also writes that its ability to meet its compute obligations depends on its ability to generate significant revenue growth.

Anthropic is organized as a public benefit corporation, which allows it to weigh the impact on society alongside shareholder interests. Its debut is the largest for a public benefit corporation and the first for a company focused only on generative AI. At an investor meeting last week, CEO Dario Amodei said developing safeguards was the limiting factor in deploying its AI models. "We don't want these agents to run wild," he said.

The company also faces opposition to new data centers. Residents near a data center under construction for Anthropic in West Virginia have complained about flooding, and labor groups including National Nurses United urged retirement funds to stay away from the IPO.

Anthropic was founded nearly six years ago by former OpenAI employees. OpenAI was long expected to go public first, but executive departures, shifting priorities and legal troubles slowed its plans.

item.title: Microsoft Is Retiring To Do in June 2027, and Personal Users Get No Replacement (2027)
item.description:
Microsoft is retiring Microsoft To Do. All To Do apps will stop working on June 30, 2027, and tasks will not move to Planner, the app Microsoft wants users to switch to. Users with a personal Microsoft account cannot use Planner at all.

Microsoft confirmed the plan in an announcement about unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365 during its Ignite conference, and in a support document. The To Do service, its APIs and sync support will retire later, on separate timelines.

What Happens to Microsoft To Do Tasks

Existing To Do tasks and lists stay accessible through Planner until June 30, 2027, but that access ends with the apps. Microsoft says the retirement date does not itself delete the underlying data.

Planner does not do everything To Do does. Microsoft lists these gaps:

  • no native Windows or Mac desktop app is planned to replace To Do
  • tasks in the Planner private plan do not support file attachments
  • Planner has no equivalent to To Do list groups
  • printing and emailing lists, as To Do does, are not currently planned

Microsoft calls the new system "a unified platform for people and agents across Microsoft 365" that makes accessing Planner through Copilot, Cowork and Autopilot easier.

What Personal Users Can Do

Personal account holders, including Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers, have no Microsoft replacement. Microsoft advises them to choose another task management app and prepare to export their data:

  1. Keep using To Do for now. The apps work until June 30, 2027.
  2. Pick a replacement task app.
  3. Export your tasks once Microsoft publishes its export instructions, which are not available yet.
  4. Check that the new app can import the exported file, because the export will not necessarily work in other apps.

Business and education users can move to Planner, but they will have to rebuild their lists, since nothing migrates automatically.

To Do was built by the team behind Wunderlist, which Microsoft bought in 2015 for between $100 million and $200 million. Microsoft later shut down Wunderlist and moved its users to To Do. The app runs on the web, Windows 11, iOS and Android, and syncs tasks with Outlook.

Some users reacted to the announcement with criticism, with one calling it "a mess" and another asking whether To Do could be released as an open source project.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Is Retiring To Do in June 2027, and Personal Users Get No Replacement appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: GTA VI Launches at 30 FPS on Every Console, and Rockstar Says the PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough (2026)
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI is out now on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, 13 years after Grand Theft Auto V. It runs at 30 frames per second on every console, including the PS5 Pro, and Rockstar says the hardware is the reason.

Most big console games now offer a 60 or 40 fps performance mode. GTA VI does not, which disappoints players who paid for the more powerful PS5 Pro, which currently sells for $899.99.

Why GTA VI Runs at 30 FPS on PS5 Pro

Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers explained the decision in an interview. According to Chambers:

  • the base version of the game uses ray traced reflections and global illumination on every console
  • the PS5 Pro adds ray traced shadows and sharper images through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)
  • the PS5 Pro's upgraded graphics processor is used to increase visual quality, not frame rate

Head of development Rob Nelson put it more simply. "It wouldn't have been acceptable to anybody," he said about a performance mode. According to Nelson, the technical team saw no way to add one without heavy compromises. "Too much, too much," he said.

Chambers was just as direct about the processor. "While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," he said.

The game world is dense, with large numbers of vehicles, characters and reactive foliage, and the simulation behind it is what holds back the frame rate. The game also has to run on the Xbox Series S, the least powerful current console.

No PC Version Yet

GTA VI is a console exclusive at launch. Rockstar has not announced a release date for a PC version.

The game is also digital only in practice. Even the boxed edition contains only a download code, and the download is up to 212 GB depending on the console. Pre-loads opened on November 10, so players who pre-ordered could start playing at midnight. Others have to download the full game first.

The launch follows strong early sales and reviews. GTA VI is estimated to have generated more than $1.5 billion in pre-orders, and critics have praised its recreation of Vice City and the story of its two leads, Jason and Lucia.

Rockstar has not said whether a future update could add a performance mode on consoles.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post GTA VI Launches at 30 FPS on Every Console, and Rockstar Says the PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Starts Upgrading Windows 11 PCs to Version 26H2 Automatically (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has started upgrading Windows 11 PCs to version 26H2 automatically. The rollout began on November 18 and covers personal devices and business devices that are not managed by an IT department, running Windows 11 version 24H2 or 25H2.

Until now, users had to check for updates manually to get 26H2. That option has been available on all eligible devices since late October. As the phased rollout continues, more devices will upgrade on their own, depending on each device's Windows Update settings.

"Starting November 18, we are taking the next step in version 26H2's phased rollout to make it easier to get the update," Microsoft said on its release health dashboard. "We are gradually expanding automatic delivery, beginning with devices running Windows 11, versions 24H2 and 25H2, that are not managed by IT departments."

What Windows 11 26H2 Changes

Windows 11 26H2, also called the Windows 11 2026 Update, became generally available in September 2026. It is delivered as an enablement package rather than a full reinstall of Windows. "This new version contains all the recently announced features in Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2. It's delivered using servicing technology, providing a fast installation experience," Microsoft says.

Because the upgrade depends on each device's Windows Update settings, not every PC receives it at the same time. Devices managed by IT departments are not part of this automatic rollout and keep following the update policies their administrators set.

The upgrade also resets the support clock. Key dates for 26H2:

  • automatic delivery to unmanaged devices started on November 18, 2026
  • manual installation has been available to all eligible devices since late October 2026
  • support ends in October 2029, less than three years from now

How to Install Windows 11 26H2 Now

Users who do not want to wait for the automatic upgrade can install 26H2 manually:

  1. Check your current version under Settings, System, About. If it already says 26H2, there is nothing to do.
  2. Open Settings and go to Windows Update.
  3. Select Check for Windows updates.
  4. Install Windows 11, version 26H2 when it appears.
  5. To get future updates as early as possible, turn on "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available."

Last month, Microsoft warned customers to upgrade devices running unsupported versions of Windows, because they will stop receiving security updates after next year's Windows Update certificate rotation.

The automatic rollout arrives during a difficult month for Windows updates. Microsoft has confirmed activation failures and printing problems after the November security updates, and this week said the November hotpatch breaks the installation and launch of some apps on devices running Windows 11 24H2 and later. Microsoft has not said when the automatic rollout will reach every eligible device.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Starts Upgrading Windows 11 PCs to Version 26H2 Automatically appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Google Play Will Block App Updates That Don't Work Properly on Foldables From April (2027)
item.description:
Google will require Android apps on Google Play to work properly on foldable phones. Under new adaptive app quality requirements that take effect in April 2027, apps that fall short will no longer be able to publish or update on Google Play and may become harder to find in the store.

Google says owners of premium foldable phones expect their apps to switch smoothly between the folded and unfolded screens. The company counts more than 580 million large-screen Android devices in use today, from foldables and tablets to Amazon's Alexa tablets, Googlebook laptops and Android XR devices like the XREAL Aura.

It recommends that developers build adaptive layouts with modern UI toolkits like Jetpack Compose, so the same app scales from phones to foldables and tablets.

What Android Apps Must Do on Foldables

Apps will need to meet at least Tier 3, called "adaptive ready," of Android's adaptive app quality guidelines for foldables. In practice, that means apps have to:

  • fill the foldable's full display without letterboxing or compatibility modes
  • keep text and playback state when the device is rotated, folded or unfolded
  • support multi window use
  • target API level 37 (Android 17), which removes the developer opt outs for orientation and resizing restrictions on large screens

Tier 2 ("adaptive optimized") and Tier 1 ("adaptive differentiated") offer a better experience on foldables. Google says Play's quality framework will gradually expand to include those tiers across foldables, tablets, Googlebooks and Android XR. Apps that reach them can get store badges, editorial spotlights and enhanced merchandising on Google Play.

Google Play Foldable Requirements Timeline

The changes arrive in stages:

  1. Now: developers can upload foldable screenshots in Play Console, showing both the inner and outer screens.
  2. April 2027: Tier 3 becomes the minimum for apps that publish or update, and listings need 3 foldable screenshots in addition to the 2 standard phone screenshots.
  3. August 2027: separate large screen requirements apply to games, which Google has published as a dedicated set of quality rules for game developers.

Google points developers to the Android CLI and the Android Emulator to capture screenshots that are ready for Play Console, so developers without a foldable device can still meet the screenshot requirement.

Older apps that are not updated stay available to download, but they may have reduced visibility on the store. Screenshots can come from physical devices or the Android Emulator.

For users, the change means fewer stretched, letterboxed or broken apps on the inner screens of foldable phones, at least among apps that are still updated. Google says it is also working on future requirements for tablets, Chromebooks and other large screen devices.

Google will require Android apps on Google Play to work properly on foldable phones. Under new adaptive app quality requirements that take effect in April 2027, apps that fall short will no longer be able to publish or update on Google Play and may become harder to find in the store.

Google says owners of premium foldable phones expect their apps to switch smoothly between the folded and unfolded screens. The company counts more than 580 million large-screen Android devices in use today, from foldables and tablets to Amazon's Alexa tablets, Googlebook laptops and Android XR devices like the XREAL Aura.

It recommends that developers build adaptive layouts with modern UI toolkits like Jetpack Compose, so the same app scales from phones to foldables and tablets.

Apps will need to meet at least Tier 3, called "adaptive ready," of Android's adaptive app quality guidelines for foldables. In practice, that means apps have to:

  • fill the foldable's full display without letterboxing or compatibility modes
  • keep text and playback state when the device is rotated, folded or unfolded
  • support multi window use
  • target API level 37 (Android 17), which removes the developer opt outs for orientation and resizing restrictions on large screens

Tier 2 ("adaptive optimized") and Tier 1 ("adaptive differentiated") offer a better experience on foldables. Google says Play's quality framework will gradually expand to include those tiers across foldables, tablets, Googlebooks and Android XR. Apps that reach them can get store badges, editorial spotlights and enhanced merchandising on Google Play.

The changes arrive in stages:

  1. Now: developers can upload foldable screenshots in Play Console, showing both the inner and outer screens.
  2. April 2027: Tier 3 becomes the minimum for apps that publish or update, and listings need 3 foldable screenshots in addition to the 2 standard phone screenshots.
  3. August 2027: separate large screen requirements apply to games, which Google has published as a dedicated set of quality rules for game developers.

Google points developers to the Android CLI and the Android Emulator to capture screenshots that are ready for Play Console, so developers without a foldable device can still meet the screenshot requirement.

Older apps that are not updated stay available to download, but they may have reduced visibility on the store. Screenshots can come from physical devices or the Android Emulator.

item.title: UK Court Forces Government to Confirm It Ordered Apple to Open iCloud Encryption (2026)
item.description:
The UK's Investigatory Powers Tribunal has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice. The order has been widely reported as demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data. The tribunal rejected the Home Office's argument that confirming the notice exists would damage national security.

The Home Office had followed its usual "neither confirm nor deny" policy on the case. The three judges pointed to extensive public reporting, statements by US officials and media briefings that they concluded the UK government had authorized.

What the Apple Backdoor Ruling Means

A Technical Capability Notice is issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016. It forces companies to make technical changes that support the UK government's legal surveillance powers. The ruling confirms only that the notice exists. Its exact demands stay secret for now.

"Although there has been extensive media coverage and public statements about the existence of a technical capability notice, there has been no publication of its precise content," the judgment states.

The judges agreed that disclosing all the material would harm national security, but said not every detail has to stay secret, and that the exact boundaries cannot be set yet.

The case so far:

  • January 2025: the Home Office demands an iCloud backdoor, which becomes public in February 2025
  • February 2025: Apple removes Advanced Data Protection for UK users
  • August 2025: US officials say the UK agreed to drop its demand for access to Americans' encrypted data
  • October 2025: the UK reportedly replaces the original notice with a new order focused on British users
  • July 2026: Apple files a second legal challenge after its first was dismissed
  • first half of 2027: a full hearing is planned

Advanced Data Protection in the UK

Advanced Data Protection extends end to end encryption to more iCloud data, including backups, photos and notes. Only the user's trusted devices hold the keys, so Apple cannot decrypt that data for investigators.

Without it, the data is still encrypted, but Apple holds the keys and can hand content over in response to valid legal demands. Some categories stay end to end encrypted either way. The feature is still available in the US.

A government spokesperson defended the powers. "The right to privacy is crucial but it should not come at the expense of the safety of the British public," the spokesperson said, adding that the government "never has direct access to a company's communications systems or data" and that the notice "simply requires that they maintain the ability" to help police.

The proceedings also include a separate challenge to the notice regime from Liberty, Privacy International and two individuals. Apple has not publicly commented on the ruling.

item.title: Valve Says Rising Memory Costs Leave Steam Machine Prices Uncertain and Closes the 2TB Waitlist (2026)
item.description:
Valve says the Steam Machine could get more expensive. In an update on its hardware blog, the company said rising memory and storage costs mean it does not yet know the number of units it can build or what it will charge for them.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them," Valve wrote.

Steam Machine Stock: 512GB vs 2TB

There is good news for buyers of the cheaper model. Valve has fulfilled every reservation for the 512GB Steam Machine, and there is stock left over, so anyone can now buy one without a reservation or a waitlist. The 2TB model is a different story:

  • Valve has sent purchase invitations to every 2TB reservation holder
  • the 2TB waitlist is longer than current production and is closed to new signups
  • people already on the waitlist keep their place but have no guarantee of a machine
  • Valve says it will build fewer 2TB units than planned, even once it gets more parts

People on the 2TB waitlist can buy the 512GB model instead, but they lose their place in line if they do. When the 512GB model sells out, Valve will mark it as out of stock without opening a new waitlist. The company expects to share more about 2TB supply in January.

Why Steam Machine Prices May Rise

The Steam Machine launched about five months ago at $1,049 for the 512GB model and $1,349 for the 2TB model, both without a controller. Apart from storage, the two models are identical, with a six core Zen 4 processor, RDNA 3 graphics with 8GB of video memory and 16GB of system memory.

Those prices were based on what Valve paid for components in the six months before launch, and the company has said it already sells the Steam Machine at cost. That leaves little room to absorb further increases in RAM and SSD prices, which have climbed as demand from AI data centers grows.

Valve has raised hardware prices before. In June, it pointed to the Steam Deck OLED price increases, $240 for the 512GB model and $300 for the 1TB model, as a rough guide to how far the Steam Machine's price had already climbed from its original target.

Demand for the Steam Machine was high enough that Valve used a randomized lottery to hand out reservations. Valve has not said whether a price increase would apply to the 512GB model, the 2TB model or both.

item.title: Windows 11 KB5132057 Brings a New Search That Can Change Settings, the Last Preview Update of (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has released KB5132057, the last non-security preview update for Windows 11 in 2026. The headline change is a rebuilt Windows Search that shows results in a single list, handles typos better and can complete simple tasks without opening Settings.

KB5132057 is optional for now. Users can install it right away from Windows Update, or wait until the changes arrive with the December Patch Tuesday update.

Microsoft is pausing preview updates over the holidays, so there will be no further non-security preview update in late November or December. The normal cycle resumes in January 2027.

The New Windows Search

Microsoft describes the new search as having "a streamlined design, improved performance, and new ways to complete tasks directly from search." Results now appear in one simplified list, and Microsoft says the new experience also uses memory more efficiently.

The biggest addition is inline actions. From the search box, users can:

  • turn on dark mode or Bluetooth
  • adjust screen brightness or mute the device
  • arrange open windows
  • call or text contacts, ring a lost phone or turn on Do Not Disturb, if an Android phone is connected through Phone Link

Search results are also richer. Files can be previewed directly in the results, along with details such as when a file was last modified, where it is saved and who created it. Quick answers about weather, stocks and facts appear without leaving search, and Windows now recognizes typos and synonyms, so a search term does not have to be an exact match. The new search is available in English first.

Other Changes in KB5132057

The update brings a long list of smaller improvements:

  • Windows Hello: facial recognition can briefly brighten the screen to help users sign in in a dark room. The option is under Settings, Accounts, Sign-in options, Facial recognition (Windows Hello).
  • Run dialog: a redesigned Run dialog can be turned on under Settings, System, Advanced.
  • File Explorer: search from This PC is now indexer-based, which makes it much faster.
  • XBOX mode: Quick settings are now available in the Gaming Task View navigation bar.
  • Screen capture: the border shown during a capture changes from yellow to red.
  • Accessibility: a new Pointer indicator helps people with low vision find the mouse pointer, toggled with Windows + Ctrl + Shift + X. Live captions can now caption system audio, microphone audio or both.
  • Sign-in: web sign-in now works on Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices, using a FIDO2 security key, a passkey on a phone or a Temporary Access Pass.

The update also fixes boot failures and TPM initialization errors on some Arm-based systems that use a TPM 2.0 Command Response Buffer interface, and an issue that added an extra character at the start of Japanese text in RemoteApp applications.

Most of the new features, including the new search, roll out gradually. Installing KB5132057 does not guarantee that every feature appears right away.

How to Install KB5132057

  1. Open Settings and go to Windows Update.
  2. Select Check for updates.
  3. Download and install KB5132057 when it appears under the optional updates.
  4. Restart the PC when prompted.

Users who prefer to wait can skip the optional update. The same changes will be included in the December security update.

item.title: Signal Blocks Siri, Gemini and Other AI Agents From Reading Your Messages (2026)
item.description:
Signal has started blocking the AI agents built into iOS and Android from reading its users' messages. Updates to the encrypted messaging app now prevent screenshots in the app on iOS 27, and block AI assistants that try to capture Signal's screen on Android, unless the user turns the protection off.

Signal says the step is needed because Google and Apple are building agentic features deep into their operating systems. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," the company wrote in a blog post announcing the change.

Why Signal Is Blocking AI Agents

According to Signal, these OS-level agents "scan" the information on the screen to answer questions and complete tasks. When a Signal chat is open, the messages are captured and handed to the agent, and from there they can end up in a local database or on a remote server.

"All of this is outside of Signal's control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation," Signal said.

The company already took a similar step on Windows. Last year, Signal turned on screenshot blocking by default to stop Microsoft's Recall feature from taking and storing screenshots of Signal messages on Windows 11.

Signal calls the new OS integrations "an existential threat" to its ability to guarantee privacy. Its encryption protocol and open source code protect messages in transit, but they cannot protect content that an operating system agent reads directly from the screen.

What Changes for Users

  • iOS 27: screenshots are blocked inside the Signal app by default.
  • Android: Signal blocks screen capture when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen.
  • Opt-out: users who want to take screenshots can turn the protection off in Signal's settings. Signal warns that doing so can expose their own and their contacts' messages to AI agents.
  • macOS: no protection yet. Signal says the tools to build it without breaking the app do not exist.

Signal admits the fix is incomplete. Blocking screenshots does not stop other ways an AI agent could reach app data, such as reading content stored on the device through the file system.

Signal calls it "a serious problem" that it and other app developers "lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy." It says Google, Apple and Microsoft do not give developers an easy way to restrict AI data access "without making drastic compromises to the core user experience."

Signal is calling on the three companies to provide simple technical tools and accurate documentation so developers can keep AI agents away from sensitive app data. It also wants protection against third-party agents, such as Meta's Muse, that use accessibility permissions to read other apps. Signal says Google and Apple are talking with it about how these systems should work with privacy-focused apps, and that it hopes to share more soon.

item.title: Amazon Warns New Yorkers of Up to $5 Higher Delivery Costs Over Driver Employment Bill (2026)
item.description:
Amazon is warning customers in New York City that their deliveries could cost up to $5 more per order if a proposed labor bill becomes law. The company is showing the message in its app and on its website, next to its Black Friday deals.

The bill, called the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would force Amazon to directly employ the drivers who deliver its packages in the city, instead of outsourcing them to contractors.

What the Delivery Protection Act Would Change

Today, the driver who brings an Amazon package often wears an Amazon vest and drives an Amazon van, but works for one of the small companies Amazon calls Delivery Service Partners. Under the New York City Council bill, Amazon would have to put drivers who regularly deliver from its stations in the five boroughs on its own payroll if it wants to keep running those stations.

The key points of the bill:

  • drivers who regularly deliver packages from Amazon's city delivery stations would become Amazon employees
  • part-time drivers are included if they do more than eight hours of delivery work in any 30-day period
  • workers who sort packages at the stations are covered too
  • if Amazon ends a contract to comply and the partner lays off its drivers, Amazon must offer those drivers their old jobs first, on terms at least as good as before

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani supports the bill. He argues that subcontracting lets Amazon avoid responsibility for the people who deliver its packages.

Amazon's Campaign Against the Bill

Amazon says the legislation threatens more than 40 delivery businesses it works with in the city and the jobs of their more than 5,000 employees. The company says it would consider moving its delivery stations outside the city, which could mean higher prices and slower deliveries for New Yorkers.

The pop-up in Amazon's app and on its website warns of higher delivery costs of up to $5 per order. An "Act now" button takes shoppers to a prewritten message that asks their council member to oppose the bill. Amazon has not explained how it arrived at the $5 figure, and the bill itself does not contain any per-order charge.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin responded sharply. "If Amazon thinks this deceptive campaign will effectively threaten New Yorkers and intimidate this City Council, they are dead wrong," she said.

What Happens Next

The bill still has to pass the City Council before it can become law. Until then, the $5 increase is Amazon's warning, not an actual price change, and nothing changes for customers' orders today.

The fight is a test of how far cities can go in regulating the gig-style contractor model that large delivery companies rely on. Amazon is using its own storefront, during one of its busiest shopping weeks of the year, to put pressure on lawmakers. Customers in New York who see the pop-up can ignore it, use the "Act now" button, or contact their council member directly with their own view.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Makes $3.79 Billion on Day One, the Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever (2026)
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, according to Rockstar Games and its parent company Take-Two Interactive. The company says that makes it the biggest entertainment launch in history, ahead of any game, film or other release.

Rockstar also confirmed that the game sold 32.5 million units before release, a new pre-order record across all platforms. The game launched on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Sam Houser, President and Founder of Rockstar Games. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you."

GTA VI Launch in Numbers

The $3.79 billion figure is based on company estimates of worldwide retail sales through the end of November 19. The key numbers from the launch:

  • $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales
  • 32.5 million units sold before release, a record across all platforms
  • 99 on Metacritic, tying The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time from 1998 as the highest-rated game ever
  • 61% of active US PlayStation 5 owners and 56% of active Xbox owners worldwide played it on launch day, according to Circana
  • 8 hours and 33 minutes of average play time on PS5 that day, and 8 hours and 14 minutes on Xbox

For comparison, Grand Theft Auto V sold 11.21 million copies in its first 24 hours. GTA VI's pre-release sales alone are nearly three times that. Rockstar says GTA V has sold-in nearly 235 million units to date, and the series as a whole nearly 480 million.

item.title: Windows 11 Tests a Fix for Bluetooth Headphones Losing Audio Quality When the Mic Turns On (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is testing a fix for one of the oldest audio complaints on Windows: Bluetooth headphones that suddenly sound worse the moment an app turns on the microphone. New Windows 11 preview builds let newer Bluetooth headsets keep playing full-quality stereo audio while the microphone is in use.

The change is available to Windows Insiders in the Beta and Experimental channels, in builds released on Friday.

Why Bluetooth Audio Drops in Quality on Windows

Classic Bluetooth headphones use two different profiles. The headphone profile, called A2DP, plays high-quality stereo sound but only works in one direction. When an app or game activates the headset's microphone, Windows switches to the headset profile, also called hands-free, which handles audio in both directions. Because bandwidth is limited in two-way mode, the sound quality drops to something closer to a phone call.

That is why music or game audio often turns muffled and flat when a voice call starts, when someone joins game chat, or when voice typing is turned on.

Full Stereo With the Microphone On

The fix relies on Bluetooth LE Audio, the newer Bluetooth audio standard. With the new builds, LE Audio devices can play full stereo audio and use the microphone at the same time.

"Bluetooth LE Audio devices can now play at full-range stereo fidelity while also using the device's microphone, ensuring you continue to hear great audio quality when in game chat, in a voice call, using voice typing, or using voice chat in Copilot Chat," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines.

What users need for the improvement:

  • a Windows 11 PC on a current Beta or Experimental channel build
  • a Bluetooth LE Audio device, such as headphones, earbuds or a speaker, that supports 48kHz playback
  • a PC that supports Super Wideband Stereo

Older Bluetooth headsets that do not support LE Audio will keep switching to the lower-quality headset profile when the microphone is in use.

How to Turn It On

On a supported PC with an LE Audio device connected:

  1. Open Settings and go to System, then Sound.
  2. Under Output, select your Bluetooth device.
  3. Open Output settings and find the Format option for when the microphone is active.
  4. Choose 2 channels, 16 bit, 48000Hz.

The fix is part of a run of audio repairs from Microsoft. Earlier this month, the company fixed a problem that stopped USB Audio Class 1.0 devices from starting or producing sound on some systems after security updates released since September 2026.

Microsoft has not said when the Bluetooth improvement will reach the stable version of Windows 11. Features tested in the Beta and Experimental channels usually reach all users later, after the testing phase ends.

item.title: Oregon and Virginia Sue SpaceX Over Grok Sexual Deepfakes (2026)
item.description:
The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing SpaceX over its Grok AI chatbot. The states accuse the company of violating consumer protection laws by misleading users about how safe its generative AI tools are and how seriously it worked to stop child sexual abuse material and nonconsensual intimate images from spreading on its platforms.

Each state filed its own complaint in its own state court on Monday: Virginia in the circuit court for the city of Richmond, Oregon in Multnomah County circuit court. Both suits name SpaceX and X Corp., the SpaceX subsidiary that runs the social network X. SpaceX acquired xAI, the maker of Grok and the parent company of X Corp., in February.

What the States Allege

Last winter, users on X prompted Grok in large numbers to create sexualized images of women and minors. The states argue that this was the result of decisions made by the company. According to the complaints:

  • Grok's creators ignored industry safety standards and deliberately used weak safeguards to attract more users
  • new Grok models were not put through enough third-party evaluations before release
  • Grok's safety prompts told it to "assume good intent" and said the terms "teenage" and "girl" do "not necessarily imply underage"
  • tens of thousands of reports went to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children's CyberTipline without key information, which left the Center unable to act on them 90 percent of the time

Virginia says its investigators tested Grok shortly before filing and found its image safeguards "inconsistent and ineffective." The chatbot explained which words triggered its filters and helped investigators write prompts to get past moderation. "At no point," the complaint says, "did Grok ask whether (a) the image uploaded was of a real person, or (b) whether the user had the person's consent to use or modify the photo."

Both states say this contradicts assurances a SpaceX official gave at a New York City Council hearing in October.

What the States Want

The attorneys general are asking for civil penalties and attorneys' fees. They also point to Meta's settlement this summer with 51 US states and territories over alleged failures to protect minors as an example of how cases like this can force companies to make broad product changes.

"It's no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material, because the lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug," said Oregon attorney general Dan Rayfield.

Virginia attorney general Jay Jones said the states worked together and hired an outside law firm because their offices have limited resources. "Your size and your scope shouldn't excuse the fact that you have to play by the rules," he said.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The cases add to other lawsuits against Musk's companies over similar issues, including suits from the city of Baltimore and from teenagers in Tennessee.

item.title: Proton Drive Can Now Move Your Files Out of Google Drive Automatically (2026)
item.description:
Proton has added a way to move files from Google Drive to Proton Drive in one step. The new Easy Switch feature for Proton Drive copies a user's files in the background, so there is no need to download everything to a computer and upload it again.

The Swiss company already offered Easy Switch for email. Earlier this year, it launched tools that move emails, contacts and calendars from Google, Microsoft and other providers into Proton Mail. The new feature applies the same idea to cloud storage.

How Easy Switch for Proton Drive Works

Easy Switch sits in the left navigation of Proton Drive on the web. Users select their Google Drive account, and the tool takes over from there. Files go straight from Google's servers to Proton's, so the import does not depend on how much free space the user's computer has.

Users can keep working in Proton Drive during the transfer and check progress from the Drive homepage or from settings. Proton sends an email once the import is done. The feature is rolling out gradually, so some accounts may not see it yet.

What Proton says the tool does:

  • keeps the same folder structure that the files had in Google Drive
  • converts Google Docs files to DOCX and Google Sheets files to XLSX, to keep formatting and design intact
  • runs in the background, server to server, without manual downloading and re-uploading
  • works on all Proton Drive plans, including the free plan, through the web interface

Proton says moving files was one of the main obstacles for people who wanted to leave Google, and that Easy Switch automates the whole process in a few clicks.

Proton's Privacy Pitch

Proton is marketing the feature as a privacy upgrade. The company points out that Google encrypts files stored in Google Drive but keeps the keys itself. Proton Drive uses end-to-end encryption, which Proton says means only the account owner can open the files. Proton also says it does not use customer files to train AI models.

Check Your Storage Before Switching

Storage is the main thing to check before starting a migration. The free plans differ:

  • Google Drive free: 15GB
  • Proton Drive free: 5GB
  • Proton Drive paid: 200GB for $2.50 per month

Users with more than 5GB in Google Drive will need a paid Proton plan to move everything, or they will have to choose which files to bring over. Since the transfer copies files, it is also worth checking that everything arrived in Proton Drive before deleting anything from Google Drive.

To use Easy Switch, sign in to Proton Drive in a web browser, select Easy Switch in the left navigation and choose the Google Drive account to import. Proton says support starts with Google Drive. Users who already moved their Gmail with Easy Switch in Proton Mail can follow the same steps for their files.

item.title: Unreal Engine 6 Drops Blueprints as Epic Bets on AI to Convert Projects (2026)
item.description:
Epic Games has dropped Blueprints from Unreal Engine 6. The visual scripting system, which has been a standard part of Unreal for years, will not be included in Unreal Engine 6 or its Early Access release. Epic says AI will help developers move their existing projects over instead.

Epic Games executive vice president of development Marcus Wassmer announced the change in a post on the Unreal Engine website. "UE6, including UE6 Early Access, won't include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework. Gameplay will be built in Verse and on the new Scene Graph framework," he wrote.

A Change of Plan

This reverses what Epic said earlier this year. In June, the company said Blueprints and Actors would exist alongside the new system in UE6 Early Access and 6.0, so that UE5 projects could be upgraded step by step while Scene Graph matured.

Wassmer said AI changed that plan. According to the post, Epic now expects AI to help with converting UE5 projects to UE6, or to make the process fully automatic. "That also means we can deliver UE6 on time (or sooner!) while meeting its design goals: a new data model, a Verse-first architecture, modularity, and AI operability," he wrote.

What the change means for developers:

  • Unreal Engine 6 gameplay is built in Verse, Epic's programming language, on the Scene Graph framework
  • Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework are not part of UE6 or UE6 Early Access
  • Blueprints are not being removed from Unreal Engine 5
  • Epic says UE5 projects will still be easy to convert, with AI doing the bulk of the work

Wassmer pointed to the falling cost of AI task completion and to Epic's own work converting the Blueprint library of Fortnite to Verse with AI assistance, which he described as going well.

Why Developers Are Worried

Blueprints let designers and artists build game logic by connecting visual nodes instead of writing code. Without them, those developers have to learn Verse or use AI prompts to build gameplay.

Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek argued in a video that tools like Blueprints sit between beginner and expert work. "It's losing those tools that made all those designers and all those artists so powerful," he said.

At least one studio is already reacting. Freshly Baked Games, the team behind the first-person RPG Queen's Domain, which was built with Unreal Engine, plans to switch engines for its next project because of Unreal's move toward AI. Co-developer Eric Berger said Blueprints were a major part of the workflow on Queen's Domain.

Epic has not given a release date for Unreal Engine 6 Early Access. Developers on UE5 can keep using Blueprints for now.

item.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Less Than Two Weeks After His Resignation (2026)
item.description:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, less than two weeks after he resigned. The company's board voted unanimously to bring him back, and he also returns as a member of the board, effective immediately.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, stepped down earlier this month after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a Singapore-based businesswoman whom US intelligence suspected of working for China's Ministry of State Security. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO. Last week, board chair Harvey C. Jones said the company had no plans to reinstate Huang.

Why the Board Changed Its Mind

In its announcement, Nvidia said the board voted after "a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA."

The company also said the board "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." Huang has a close relationship with US President Donald Trump, who backed calls for his return.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," said Jones, who remains board chair. Kress returns to her role as chief financial officer.

Huang thanked the board, his staff and his family. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," he said. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

The Investigation Continues

Huang's return does not end the inquiry into the reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Nvidia says:

  • a committee made up only of independent directors is investigating, with independent counsel, and that investigation "will proceed to conclusion"
  • Huang "fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it"
  • a new National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors will oversee trade compliance and national security risks
  • the company is searching for a new Chief Compliance Officer, who will oversee compliance across Nvidia
  • Nvidia will keep cooperating with ongoing government investigations and inquiries

Markets Welcome the Return

Investors reacted quickly. Nvidia lost billions of dollars in market value when Huang's resignation was announced, and its shares jumped after the board announced his return.

The board had faced pressure from tech industry leaders to bring Huang back after he left. The reinstatement settles the leadership question for now, but the outcome of the independent investigation is still open.

item.title: Microsoft's Final Outage Report Blames a July Bug and Confirms Some Emails Never Arrived (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has published its final report on the Microsoft 365 outage that took down Outlook and other services for millions of users in November. The report confirms that a software defect introduced in July caused the outage, and that some emails were never delivered.

The outage began on November 12 and was not fully resolved until November 14. At its worst point, more than 80 percent of Microsoft's North American gateway servers were unresponsive.

What Caused the Outage

According to Microsoft, a combination of factors brought the service down:

  • a Windows code change from July contained a defect in Microsoft's gateway server configuration. It ran worldwide for more than three months before it caused problems.
  • about 14% of server capacity was offline for unrelated reasons
  • planned maintenance and a shift of Teams traffic onto Exchange Online gateways added load
  • peak traffic in North America, as US users came online, pushed the gateways over the edge

When servers failed, traffic was moved to healthy servers around the world, which spread the problem instead of containing it. A separate mechanism that should have stopped the failure from spreading also failed.

Recovery took time because engineers first had to find a defect that had gone unnoticed for months. Servers then had to be restarted before the fix could be applied, and restarted again to activate it. Microsoft says the defect affected its own gateway servers, not standard Windows installations.

Some Emails Never Arrived

item.title: Gemini for Mac Can Now Click, Type and Run Your Desktop Apps for You (2026)
item.description:
Google is giving the Gemini app on Mac the ability to operate desktop apps on its own. The new Computer Use feature lets Gemini click, type and move between local apps and websites to complete multi-step tasks for the user.

Computer Use is rolling out now in US English for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers on Mac.

How Computer Use Works

Google launched its native Gemini app for macOS earlier this year. It first added an Option + Space shortcut, then voice dictation and the ability to reason about what is on the screen. The app's Task feature could already read local files and combine them with Connected Apps such as Gmail and Google Calendar, but it could not operate software that has no built-in connector.

That changes with the update. Users add @Computer use to a prompt to hand off a job that moves between local apps and websites. Gemini then does the work in an isolated background window, with a live preview shown in the chat. The user's main screen and cursor stay free during that time.

Google is also adding new Desktop app integrations under Customize, Connectors. They include:

  • Blender
  • Autodesk Fusion
  • Git and Obsidian, which were already supported

Safety Controls

An AI that clicks and types on a computer raises obvious questions about control. Google says users decide what Gemini can do:

  • users choose which apps Gemini is allowed to use
  • a task can be stopped with one click
  • Gemini pauses for logins, payments and confirmation before any sensitive action

Mac First, Windows Later

The Mac app keeps getting Google's newest desktop AI tools first. Google launched a dedicated Gemini app for Windows in September, but Computer Use is limited to Mac for now. Google has not said when, or if, it will come to Windows or to its own Googlebook laptops.

The feature arrives as some app makers push back against OS-level AI agents. Signal, for example, now blocks AI assistants from reading its chats on iOS and Android.

Subscribers who want to try it can follow these steps:

  3. Start a task and add @Computer use to your prompt.
  4. Choose which apps Gemini may use, and watch the live preview in the chat.

item.title: Steam Awards 2026 Nominations Open With a Hall of Fame Vote for the Best Game of the Decade (2026)
item.description:
Valve has opened nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards, the tenth edition of its annual player-voted game awards. To mark the anniversary, this year's event adds a Hall of Fame category that picks the number one game of the past ten years from the Steam Game of the Year winners since 2016.

Nominations are open now and close on November 30. The nominees will be revealed and voting will begin with the start of the Steam Winter Sale on December 17.

The Hall of Fame Contenders

The Hall of Fame category is locked to ten games. In order of the award year, they are:

  • Grand Theft Auto V
  • The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
  • PUBG
  • Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
  • Red Dead Redemption 2
  • Resident Evil Village
  • Elden Ring
  • Baldur's Gate 3
  • Black Myth: Wukong
  • Hollow Knight: Silksong

Two names on the list look odd at first. Grand Theft Auto V did not come out in 2016, and The Witcher 3 did not come out in 2017. Steam did not hand out a Game of the Year award in those years, so Valve says in its FAQ that it used the winners of the "Whoooaaaaaaa, Dude!" award from 2016 and the "Choices Matter" award from 2017 instead. Grand Theft Auto V and The Witcher 3 won those awards, so they now count as the Game of the Year winners for those years.

How Nominations Work

Apart from the Hall of Fame, nominations are open. For each category, Steam shows a list of games the user has played, plus popular and recommended games they have not played. Users can also nominate any other game in any category, as long as it was released in 2026.

Valve has also added a few new categories for the tenth anniversary, inspired by categories from earlier years.

Taking part comes with a small reward: nominating games earns Steam badges.

Key Dates

  • Now until November 30: nominations are open for 2026 games in every category
  • December 17: nominees are revealed and voting begins with the Steam Winter Sale

The Hall of Fame vote is the one to watch. Steam's user base does not always vote the way critics or other award shows do, which leaves room for a surprise among the ten past winners.

Users who want to take part can nominate games through Steam until November 30. Each category suggests games the user has played, but any 2026 release can be entered.

item.title: Microsoft Deprecates Bluetooth File Transfers and the Family Safety App in Windows 11 (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has deprecated two more features in Windows 11: the ability to transfer files over Bluetooth using MTP, and the built-in Family Safety app. Both were added to Microsoft's list of deprecated Windows features this month and may be removed in a future version of the operating system.

What Is Being Deprecated

MTP over Bluetooth uses the Media Transfer Protocol to send files to, or receive files from, an external device over a Bluetooth connection. It is useful when there is no USB cable at hand, but Bluetooth transfers are slow compared to a cable or to services such as Phone Link.

The Family Safety app is the in-box Windows app for managing Microsoft family settings on the PC. Microsoft recommends that users manage their family settings on the Microsoft Family Safety website or in the Family Safety mobile app instead.

The Family Safety decision is a little surprising. Microsoft has announced plans to expand family safety features on Windows 11 in the coming months, even as it drops the dedicated app.

What Deprecation Means for Users

Deprecation does not remove a feature right away. It means Microsoft has stopped actively developing it, and that it may be removed from a future version of Windows. In practice:

  • both features keep working on current versions of Windows 11 for now
  • Microsoft no longer adds improvements to them
  • they can be removed in a later Windows release

Users who rely on either feature should plan an alternative now:

  • Instead of MTP over Bluetooth: use a USB cable, Phone Link for Android phones, or a cloud storage service to move files between devices.
  • Instead of the Family Safety app: open the Microsoft Family Safety website in a browser, or use the Family Safety app on a phone.

A Short List of Deprecations in 2026

Microsoft has deprecated only a handful of Windows features in 2026. Along with the two new entries, the year's list includes:

  • 3D Viewer
  • PowerShell 5.1
  • MTP over Bluetooth
  • the Family Safety app

The two new entries are not widely used parts of Windows. Users of the old features can keep using them for the foreseeable future, but Microsoft can remove deprecated features at any point in a later release, so switching early avoids surprises after a future feature update.

item.title: Tidal Bans AI-Generated Music and Will Remove 29 Million Songs (2026)
item.description:
Tidal is banning AI-generated music from its streaming service. Starting December 9, the company will begin removing songs it believes were made entirely with AI, which makes it the first music streaming service to ban AI-generated music from its catalog outright.

The company announced the plan on Tuesday and said it thinks the move "will resonate with both artists and listeners alike."

29 Million Songs Will Disappear

Tidal's Music Lead Robert Anderson shared the numbers behind the decision on X. According to Anderson:

  • 43% of the tracks Tidal received in the last 90 days were AI-generated
  • Tidal will remove 29 million songs by the beginning of 2027
  • that works out to roughly 80,000 to 85,000 removals per day
  • 96% of the AI-generated songs on Tidal have zero plays

The last figure shows how most AI tracks end up on streaming services: uploaded in bulk, and never listened to by anyone. Removing them is unlikely to affect what Tidal subscribers actually play.

A Step Beyond Labels

This is not Tidal's first move against AI music. In July, the company started labeling songs made entirely with AI and said it would remove tracks it found to be "fraudulent and deceptive."

Other services have taken smaller steps. Apple Music is working on AI labels for its app, and Spotify has pushed back against AI music to some degree. None of them has gone as far as banning AI-generated music outright.

The ban covers music that Tidal believes is made entirely with AI, the same group of songs it started labeling in July.

The timeline of Tidal's moves against AI music:

  • July 2026: labels for songs made entirely with AI, and removal of fraudulent and deceptive tracks
  • December 9, 2026: removals of fully AI-generated songs begin
  • Early 2027: 29 million songs removed, according to Tidal

What It Means for Listeners

For listeners who want to avoid AI music, Tidal is now the clearest choice among the big streaming services. Its catalog should soon contain music that was at least mostly made by humans.

For artists, the move takes away competition from mass-produced AI tracks that are uploaded to the service in bulk.

Whether other services follow is the open question. The scale of the problem is clear from Tidal's own numbers: when close to half of new uploads are AI-generated, labels alone do little to keep catalogs clean. Tidal subscribers will see the removals start on December 9.

item.title: New York Bans Car Subscriptions for Features Already Built Into the Vehicle (2026)
item.description:
New York is banning car makers and dealers from charging subscription fees to unlock features that are already built into a vehicle. Governor Kathy Hochul signed the law on Monday, and it takes effect next February.

The law targets a practice in which parts are installed at the factory but stay switched off in software until the owner pays. Hochul called pay-to-unlock pricing a "deceptive business model."

What the Law Bans

A heated seat is the clearest example. The heating elements, wiring and controls are already in the car, and running them costs the manufacturer nothing after the sale. Under the new law, a subscription for a feature is banned if it meets two tests:

  • the feature runs on equipment that was in the vehicle when it was bought or leased
  • once turned on, it works without ongoing cost or support from the manufacturer or a third party

The law defines a vehicle feature broadly as any convenience or safety function, and covers both buyers and people who lease. Monthly loan and lease payments do not count as subscriptions. Car makers also cannot charge for a software update that fixes a safety defect they must repair for free under federal rules.

In a memo, the bill's sponsors listed heated seats, entertainment options, enhanced navigation and hands-free driving as examples of charges that are spreading, and said they wanted to stop the practice before it became standard.

The Big Exceptions

Services that have real ongoing costs are not covered. The ban does not apply to:

  • navigation updates, infotainment and satellite radio
  • in-vehicle Wi-Fi, telematics and roadside assistance
  • "vehicle-connected services" that depend on cellular or other data networks
  • driver assistance and driver automation features that depend on software

The last exemption sits awkwardly with the sponsors' own examples, since hands-free driving was one of the features they named. In practice, features defined mainly by hardware face the strictest limits, while car makers can argue that other features count as connected or software-based.

Penalties and Next Steps

Violations carry a civil penalty of up to $250 per point of sale for each violation. The law does not define "point of sale" or explain how violations are counted. New York's Department of State will set those details when it writes the enforcement rules.

The bill passed the state Senate 57 to 3 and was backed by Attorney General Letitia James. It is New York's second attempt: a similar bill passed the legislature in 2025 but was vetoed.

For drivers in New York, the result is simple for features like seat heaters that need no data connection. Harder cases will come as more car functions run on shared sensors and central computers.

item.title: Capcom Will Shut Down Exoprimal in September 2027 and Pull It From Sale in March (2027)
item.description:
Capcom is shutting down Exoprimal, its online dinosaur shooter. The servers will go offline on September 29, 2027, and since the game has no offline mode, it will be unplayable after that date.

Capcom announced the shutdown in a post on the Exoprimal website. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement," the company wrote.

Shutdown Timeline

Capcom is closing the game in steps:

  • Now: the premium tiers of the Survival Pass, the game's paid battle pass, have been removed from the in-game store
  • March 30, 2027: Exoprimal is taken off sale
  • September 29, 2027: online services end and the game can no longer be played

Players who already own the game have about six months of play after the end of sales. New players have until March 30 to buy it, though the purchase would only be playable until the servers close.

A Short Life for a Live Service Game

Exoprimal launched in 2023, the same year Capcom released Resident Evil 4 and Street Fighter 6. It is a PvPvE shooter: players pick from character classes and battle each other while fending off armies of dinosaurs.

The game had a rocky start. When it was announced, it frustrated fans of Capcom's Dino Crisis series, especially since a character resembling Dino Crisis heroine Regina featured heavily in the marketing. It built a small cult following but never broke through in a crowded live service market, and much of its best content was locked behind long hours of play. By the time the servers shut down, it will have been playable for about four years.

Exoprimal joins a growing list of online-only games that disappear entirely when their servers close. Because all of its content requires a connection to Capcom's servers, there is no single-player mode that would keep the game alive after September 2027.

What Players Should Know

  • owners can keep playing until September 29, 2027
  • the paid Survival Pass tiers are already gone from the store
  • after the shutdown, the game cannot be launched or played at all

For players thinking about buying the game now, the timeline matters. Anyone who buys before March 30, 2027 will get at most a few months of play before the servers close.

The shutdown is another reminder of the risk of online-only games: when the publisher turns off the servers, the purchase stops working, no matter how much players paid for the game or its extras.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms November Windows Updates Break Some Sign-Ins and Shares a Registry Workaround (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has confirmed that the November 2026 security updates for Windows can cause authentication failures with some third-party apps and devices. The problems come from new NTLM security protections that the updates introduce, and a fix is not yet available.

The updates address CVE-2026-118737, a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime. According to Microsoft, the flaw stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to run code remotely, without user interaction, on unpatched systems.

What Breaks and Why

Microsoft says the November updates are the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements. They make sure authenticated NTLM sessions always set up a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing, which reduces exposure to relay attacks.

Some products do not handle the stricter rules. "Microsoft is aware of compatibility issues affecting some third-party apps and devices, including authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) solutions, and application packaging solutions that use NTLM authentication," the company said.

According to Microsoft, the problem occurs when a proxy device does not implement the NTLM protocol correctly, for example by setting the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its challenge message but providing an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field.

Administrators can spot affected apps and devices by these signs:

  • an NTLMSSP_CHALLENGE message with an empty "Target Info List" in network traces
  • Target Machine fields with "Not Found" values in event logs

The Temporary Workaround

Until a fix is available, Microsoft recommends these steps on affected systems:

  1. Set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm REG_DWORD value under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 to 1.
  2. Check whether the affected device or app can be configured to use Kerberos authentication, or whether the vendor offers an update that supports the new NTLM signing requirements.
  3. If neither is possible, ask the vendor for an update that follows the NTLM protocol requirements.

Microsoft warns that the registry setting is only a short-term solution and may be removed in the future. "Updating the affected product or using a compatible authentication configuration is the recommended long-term resolution," the company said. Since the setting relaxes a security protection, administrators should only apply it on systems that are actually affected.

A Difficult Month for Windows Updates

The authentication problem adds to a list of known issues with the November 2026 updates. Microsoft has already confirmed Windows activation failures and SQL Server performance problems, and it is investigating an issue that can break printing of documents with complex formatting.

The products Microsoft names are enterprise tools such as authentication proxies, single sign-on systems and application packaging solutions. Organizations that use these products should test the November updates and check with their vendors before rolling them out widely.

item.title: Google's AI Mode Can Now Read Your Wallet, With Drive Coming Next (2026)
item.description:
Google is letting its AI Mode in Search read more of users' personal data. Personal Intelligence in AI Mode can now connect to Google Wallet, and support for Google Drive will follow in the coming weeks.

Personal Intelligence arrived in AI Mode earlier this year. It pulls information from a user's Google apps to personalize answers. Google says the new connections are strictly opt-in: users have to turn them on manually, and can turn them off again later.

What AI Mode Can Do With Wallet and Drive

Robby Stein, Google's VP for Search, said a more connected Search can give users insights into their digital life. With Wallet connected, Google says AI Mode can:

  • track financial "milestones"
  • offer advice on ways to improve spending
  • help users get the most out of the benefits of the credit cards saved in Wallet

Google stresses that AI Mode can read financial data from a user's accounts, but cannot move, manage or invest money on their behalf.

Once Drive support arrives, AI Mode will be able to scan PDFs, documents and other files stored in Google Drive to add context to answers and suggest ideas.

Gemini and AI Mode Share Context

Google is also linking its two AI products more closely. In the coming weeks, users will be able to start a conversation in the Gemini app and continue it in AI Mode in Search, or the other way around.

Users could already connect their Search history to Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app. Now they will also be able to connect Gemini to AI Mode. Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode will also give more personalized answers based on a user's recent search context.

The changes coming to AI Mode:

  • Now: Google Wallet can be connected to Personal Intelligence
  • Coming weeks: Google Drive support
  • Coming weeks: conversations that move between the Gemini app and AI Mode

Privacy Considerations

The features are designed to make Search more useful, but they also give Google's AI direct access to financial information and personal documents. Users who care about privacy should think about which apps they connect.

Since everything is opt-in, nothing changes for users who do not turn the connections on. Those who try them can disconnect Wallet or Drive at a later date if they change their mind.

The move is part of Google's push to turn Search into a personal assistant built around AI Mode, even though Google has acknowledged on its latest earnings call that AI Mode still earns less money than traditional search.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google's AI Mode Can Now Read Your Wallet, With Drive Coming Next appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: WhatsApp Finally Lets You Schedule Messages Up to 14 Days Ahead (2026)
item.description:
WhatsApp is finally adding message scheduling, one of the most requested features for the messaging app. Users can now pick a time for a message to be sent, from 10 minutes to 14 days in the future.

WhatsApp announced the feature on its official blog. It is rolling out globally and should reach all users over the coming weeks, so not everyone will see it right away.

How Scheduled Messages Work

Scheduling is built into the send button. According to WhatsApp:

  • messages can be scheduled from 10 minutes to 14 days ahead
  • scheduling works in one-on-one chats and in group chats
  • texts, photos and videos can be scheduled
  • the sender can see the scheduled time and delete the message before it goes out
  • for the recipient, a scheduled message looks like any other message
  • scheduled messages remain end-to-end encrypted, like all WhatsApp messages

WhatsApp's announcement does not mention documents or contacts, so it is not clear whether those can be scheduled too. It also does not say whether scheduled messages can be edited before they are sent.

How to Schedule a Message

Once the feature reaches your account:

  1. Open the chat or group and type your message, or attach a photo or video.
  2. Press and hold the send button. WhatsApp only shows the send button once there is something to send; by default the microphone button sits in its place.
  3. Pick the date and the exact time, in hours and minutes, from the menu that appears.
  4. Confirm to schedule the message.

To cancel a scheduled message, find it in the chat, where the scheduled time is shown, and delete it before it is sent.

Catching Up With Rivals

Other messaging apps such as Telegram and Discord have offered message scheduling for a long time. WhatsApp, which has the largest user base of any messaging app and is used by close to a third of the world's population, has been behind on the feature until now.

The arrival also shows how slowly WhatsApp rolls out new features. In one test, WhatsApp version 2.26.46.82, released on November 24, did not include the scheduler yet, so a later update may be needed before it appears.

Since the rollout is gradual, users who do not see the option yet should keep WhatsApp updated through the Play Store or App Store. The feature is arriving through the coming weeks, and a newer version of the app may be needed before it appears.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post WhatsApp Finally Lets You Schedule Messages Up to 14 Days Ahead appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Mario Kart World 1.9.0 Adds Eight Remixed Courses and Two Knockout Tour Routes (2026)
item.description:
Nintendo has released version 1.9.0 of Mario Kart World for the Nintendo Switch 2. The update adds eight new courses, two new Knockout Tour routes and a revamped Replay feature, and it is available to download now.

The eight courses are not entirely new. Each one is a remixed take on an existing track, marked with a "2" in its name.

The Eight New Courses

The courses added in Mario Kart World 1.9.0 are:

  • Mario Bros. Circuit 2
  • Desert Hills 2
  • Shy Guy Bazaar 2
  • Wario Stadium 2
  • Airship Fortress 2
  • DK Pass 2
  • Koopa Troopa Beach 2
  • Salty Salty Speedway 2

The update also adds two Knockout Tour routes, Feather Rally and Lucky Cat Rally, which are available to race starting today.

Other Changes in Version 1.9.0

Nintendo has revamped the Replay feature, which lets players watch replays of past races and battles. The full list of changes is on Nintendo's support website and includes smaller touches:

  • confetti now falls during the results presentation in Grand Prix and Knockout Tour
  • players can now take the river route to Cheep Cheep Falls from DK Pass, Sky-High Sundae, Salty Salty Speedway, Starview Peak and Wario Shipyard

Nintendo also released a trailer for the update that shows each of the new courses. The remixed courses take existing tracks and give them new versions, which means returning players will recognize the settings while racing new layouts.

"The Update of 2s"

Player reactions are mixed. Fans have nicknamed version 1.9.0 the "update of 2s," pointing out that none of the eight courses is a completely new map. Most of the reactions are good-natured, though. "This update certainly has 'The Power of Two' in it," one player wrote.

Some players expect bigger additions soon. "People don't seem to realize we're getting close to a 2.0 update," one comment reads. The player expects version 2.0 to be the big update with the features fans are waiting for, along with some surprises. Nintendo has not announced a version 2.0 update.

Mario Kart World launched alongside the Nintendo Switch 2 on June 5 last year, and it is the best-selling game on the console so far. Nintendo has kept adding content through regular updates since launch.

Version 1.9.0 is available to download now on Nintendo Switch 2, and the new courses and Knockout Tour routes can be raced as soon as it is installed.
